summary.en: Search sequentially or halve a sorted interval, and compare their work.
summary.bn: একটি করে খোঁজা আর সাজানো অংশ অর্ধেক করে খোঁজার নিয়ম ও খরচ তুলনা করো।

practice.title: First occurrence in arbitrary order
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100, then a key from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: and Search key: before their inputs. Print the first matching zero-based index or -1.
hints: Return immediately when the linear scan finds equality.

practice.title: Binary search with a sortedness guard
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100, then a key in that range. Use prompts Count and values: and Search key:. Print Unsorted when any adjacent pair decreases; otherwise print a matching binary-search index or -1.
hints: Check order before calling binary, including empty and single-element arrays.

practice.title: First duplicate in a sorted array
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20, n nondecreasing ints from -100 to 100, then a key in that range. Use Count and values: and Search key: prompts. Return the first index containing the key, or -1. Reject unsorted input.
hints: After lower_bound, check both position < n and equality.

practice.title: Find an insertion position
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20, n nondecreasing ints from -100 to 100, then a key in that range. Use Count and values: and Search key: prompts. Print the first index whose value is at least the key, or n if all are smaller. Reject unsorted input.
hints: The returned position may legally equal the length, but it cannot then be read as an element.

quiz.prompt: Which search works correctly on arbitrary unsorted arrays?
quiz.explanation: A linear scan needs no ordered discard rule.

quiz.prompt: What is the necessary data precondition for the shown binary search?
options: Nondecreasing order under the same integer comparison
The count must be a power of two
The first value must be zero
quiz.explanation: Duplicates and arbitrary lengths are allowed; sortedness justifies removing one side.

quiz.prompt: The linear helper stops at the first repeated five. Which index is returned?
quiz.explanation: The first matching element is at index one, so later duplicates are not visited.

quiz.prompt: What does the binary helper's half-open interval [low, high) include?
quiz.explanation: The excluded high bound can equal count without being read as an element.

quiz.prompt: How should low change when values[middle] is smaller than key?
quiz.explanation: The tested midpoint cannot match, so removing it ensures a smaller interval.

quiz.prompt: The half-open binary interval starts empty. Which result is printed?
quiz.explanation: low equals high initially, so the loop reads no elements and reports failure.

quiz.prompt: What is the worst-case time for iterative binary search on a sorted array?
quiz.explanation: Each failed midpoint reduces the candidate interval by about half.

quiz.prompt: What does ordinary equality-return binary search promise among duplicate keys?
quiz.explanation: Its midpoint path can encounter any one of several equal entries.

quiz.prompt: Lower bound receives a key greater than every element. What position does it return?
quiz.explanation: The insertion position is count, equal to three. That position is not a readable array element.

quiz.prompt: What extra test is needed after lower_bound returns position?
options: Check position < count and equality before claiming a match
Reject every position equal to zero
quiz.explanation: Lower bound can return the end insertion position and can locate a greater value rather than an equal one.

quiz.prompt: How much time does checking sortedness before every search add?
options: No work because the prototype checks it
quiz.explanation: An adjacent-order check traverses the range, so the complete checked lookup is linear.

options: It avoids a potentially overflowing endpoint sum
quiz.explanation: Under valid ordered bounds, the difference formulation avoids adding two possibly large indices.

examQuestions.question: State the invariant and endpoint updates of the half-open iterative binary search.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Any remaining possible match lies in [low,high). Initially it is [0,count). Equality returns middle. A too-small midpoint sets low to middle plus one; a too-large midpoint sets high to middle. Each failure shrinks the interval, and low equal to high means absence. Sorted order justifies discarding each side.

#include <stdio.h>

int linear(const int values[], int count, int key)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (values[i] == key) {
            return i;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

int main(void)
{
    int a[] = {8, 5, 2, 5};
    printf("%d\n", linear(a, 4, 5));
    return 0;
}

examQuestions.question: Read n from 0 to 20, n nondecreasing ints from -100 to 100, then a key in that range. Use Count and values: and Search key: prompts. Print the first index whose value is at least the key, or n if all are smaller. Reject unsorted input.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int lower_bound(const int values[], int count, int key)
{
    int low = 0, high = count;
    while (low < high) {
        int middle = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if (values[middle] < key) {
            low = middle + 1;
        } else {
            high = middle;
        }
    }
    return low;
}

int main(void)
{
    int n;
    int values[20];
    puts("Count and values:");
    if (scanf("%d", &n) != 1 || n < 0 || n > 20) {
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (scanf("%d", &values[i]) != 1 || values[i] < -100 || values[i] > 100) {
            return 1;
        }
    }
    int key;
    puts("Search key:");
    if (scanf("%d", &key) != 1 || key < -100 || key > 100) {
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
        if (values[i - 1] > values[i]) {
            return 1;
        }
    }
    printf("%d\n", lower_bound(values, n, key));
    return 0;
}

The returned position may legally equal the length, but it cannot then be read as an element.

For input 0 0, the program prints:

Count and values:
Search key:
0
